frontier.hypothesis: H5'''' -- the last two points close iff an allocno that PREFERS hard reg 4, CONFLICTS with 103, and ranks BELOW 103 in allocno_compare order exists at zero instruction cost. That is the configuration target's own compile had (target's window has nothing in $a0, so an assigned-conflict exclusion is ruled out for it).
frontier.mechanism: prune_preferences (global.c:851-899) unions lower-priority CONFLICTING allocnos' full preferences into regs_someone_prefers[103], excluded by pass 0 of find_reg (:1012-1044). Priority = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs / live_length, so adding a reference pushes an allocno UP hard while lengthening a live range pushes it DOWN gently -- the carrier must gain liveness without gaining a reference.
frontier.next_probe: Allocno 102 (y) is the shape-compatible carrier: it already prefers $a0, lands in $v1 exactly where target keeps y, and sits only two positions above 103. Look for a form where y's LOAD stays in target's position but the conflicting allocno's range starts earlier -- e.g. y read through a pointer or an address pseudo computed before the chain, so the ADDRESS allocno carries the $a0 preference and the conflict. Verify BOTH conditions in the dump before scoring (`;; 103 conflicts:` contains the carrier AND the carrier appears AFTER 103 in the `regs to allocate` line); tmp/grind/func_8002EA24/s7/probe.sh prints exactly those lines per variant.
